questions.prompt: Which method should govern the Project's beginning of construction: off-site transformer manufacture in December 2025, or on-site pile installation in January 2026?
questions.context: The notice to proceed (December 18, 2025) is not physical work. The transformer manufacturer says custom core work began December 22, 2025 under a binding contract dated December 10, 2025, and Seller's counsel relies on this. The independent engineer dates on-site physical work to January 12, 2026 and has not reviewed the manufacturer's records. A 2025 start keeps the domestic content bonus (47.8% vs 45%) and avoids the foreign entity material assistance rules. A 2026 start raises the threshold to 50%, losing the bonus, and makes the foreign entity rules apply while the module certification and cost ratio are missing.

evidence.text: Physical manufacture of the transformer, beginning with cutting and stacking of the custom core, commenced at our facility on December 22, 2025
On-site physical work of a significant nature, beginning with pile installation for the tracker foundations, commenced on January 12, 2026.
We have not reviewed the manufacturer's records and express no opinion on the tax treatment of off-site work.
If construction is determined to have begun in 2026, the applicable threshold would be 50% and the Project would not qualify at the computed adjusted percentage.

rfis.reason: The 2025 construction start rests only on an unreviewed manufacturer letter and counsel's assertion. The independent engineer dates on-site physical work to January 12, 2026. The start year decides the domestic content threshold and whether the foreign entity rules apply.
